indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells the solver to read the synonym of dress from the bottom upwards

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: Someone puts on smart clothes in order to parade them in front of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GARB round to give BRAG; the surface reads 'dress up' as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, which is a way of showing off.

indicators.note: the clue says the two outer letters trade places, so the final letter travels to the front
the ends are the first and last letters, which are the ones exchanged in this clue

parts.note: snug means cosy, comfortable

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether some antelopes are comfortable after trading places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having swapped ends' exchanges the S and G at either end of SNUG, giving GNUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are large African antelopes.

clue.text: A certain stage in hippie revolution?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asks which phase of the hippie counter-culture movement is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters hipPIE Revolution. 'Stage' looks like a phase of history; it is a landing stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a landing stage built out over the water for boats.

clue.text: Supply initially with Charlie (drug): that leads to ruin

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word supply

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: Supplying cocaine and other drugs is the road to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is also slang for cocaine, which makes the surface read as drug-dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck or ruin it, originally to sink a ship deliberately.

parts.note: a ticking-off is a scolding, but here it means marking items with a tick one by one

explanation.surface: Some wrongdoers deserve a stern reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticking-off' reads as a telling-off, but the clue means putting ticks against each item.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists of tasks or items are worked through by ticking each one off when done.

clue.text: Pope, perhaps, is able to be a friar?

parts.note: Francis is the name of a pope, so a pope is an example of a Francis
can means is able to

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pope could also be a friar.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope Francis is the current pontiff, so 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Franciscan is a member of the religious order founded by St Francis of Assisi, whose members are friars.

parts.note: suggests something stingy, but means tiny droplets emerging as a mist

explanation.surface: A grumble that some container yields hardly anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' seems to mean almost nothing comes out; it really describes the droplets as very small.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser turns liquid medicine into a fine mist of tiny droplets to be breathed in.

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the following words

explanation.surface: Someone who organises speeches tends to repeat themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the letters spEECH Organiser joined across the word gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated back, so it is a repetition.

clue.text: Glean vice in translation of the Gospel

indicators.note: translating rewrites the text in another form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to gather vice from a translated version of the Gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' signals rearranging GLEANVICE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic is an adjective meaning relating to the Christian gospel or its preaching.

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building remodelled into a place serving excellent food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' tells you to rearrange ASTOPGRUB; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub serving high-quality food, so it is a venue for eating.

definitions.meaning: the clicking noise of disapproval or impatience
The popular short name for Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian boy king

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch tutting with irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is both a click of the tongue in annoyance and a nickname for a pharaoh.

definitions.meaning: ... means knowing or cunning, as in an ... smile
a curved structure that holds itself up across an opening

explanation.surface: Praise for an ingenious building that needs no props.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means slyly knowing; as a noun it is a curved span that bears its own weight.

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
the senior service is the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN

explanation.surface: A ship that serves every branch of the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is called the senior service as the oldest British armed force. 'Vessel' suggests a ship; it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, so it is a vessel in the sense of a pot.

clue.text: Whale, first of rorquals etc, jumping in somersault

indicators.note: letters that jump about are moved into a fresh order
first of asks for the opening letter of the word rorquals

explanation.surface: A whale leaping and turning over, along with others of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' signals rearranging WHALE, R and ETC. Rorquals are a family of whales, which keeps the surface marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is a sideways handspring, a gymnastic turn loosely called a somersault.

clue.text: Disguise with patchy colours? I don't see it myself!

definitions.meaning: said of something hidden so well that the speaker cannot spot it

explanation.surface: Someone admits they cannot spot the cleverly disguised thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Camouflage hides things by blending them into surroundings, so successful concealment goes unseen.

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether a royal trip was organised for a colonial governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governor' looks like a ruler; it is a device that controls speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor in engineering is a device that controls speed or flow, which is a regulator.

clue.text: Animals with young losing head, going under barrier

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that goes under another is written after it

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the synonym of young is taken off

parts.note: babies are the young of a family

explanation.surface: Creatures with their offspring ducking beneath a fence after one is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' trims BABIES to ABIES, and 'going under' puts it below WALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallabies are small kangaroo-like marsupials, a kind of animal.

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The self-confidence of a woman aged fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Gall is cheek or brazen nerve, a bold self-assurance.

clue.text: Avoid duty, with receding gums and broken leg

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word gums is read in the reverse direction
a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of leg are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone dodging work by pleading gum disease and a fractured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns GUMS into SMUG and 'broken' rearranges LEG into GLE. 'Duty' is customs duty, not a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To smuggle is to bring goods in secretly so as to dodge customs payments.

definitions.meaning: ..., read as two words, means economise

explanation.surface: A pessimist saying that saving resources is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless means pointless; split as USE LESS it means to consume fewer resources.

clue.text: A particular sort of English coming from this mouth?

definitions.text: A particular sort of English coming from this mouth?

parts.words: A particular sort of English coming from this mouth?
parts.note: a London-area accent is named after a river feature, and that feature is a river's mouth where it meets the sea

explanation.surface: Pointing at a speaker's mouth and naming a dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is the accent of the Thames estuary area east of London. 'Mouth' suggests a person speaking; it is a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the tidal mouth of a river, and it names a well-known English accent.

definitions.meaning: to ... wine is to heat it with spices
An island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Like the Spice Islands, a place known for seasonings.
explanation.definitionFit: To mull is to flavour drink with spices; Mull is also a Scottish island.

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors
tracts are pamphlets or leaflets

explanation.surface: A digest of what some navy pamphlets contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstracts are short summaries of the content of a paper or report.

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry after a promotion attracts no interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing.

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Such a robe can be bought for a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests money, but LB is the weight abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a long white vestment worn by clergy, so it is a garment.

definitions.meaning: a musical note lowered a semitone
a set of rooms on one floor, an apartment

explanation.surface: A message spotted inside someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means a lowered musical note and, in British use, a self-contained apartment.

clue.text: Condemned in pub for swallowing ecstasy tablet?

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other
condemned suggests something broken and unfit, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone denounced in a bar for taking an ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condemned' rearranges INPUBFOR and 'swallowing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkiller sold as tablets.

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the answer sounds like a word for the highway

parts.note: a road is the highway

explanation.surface: A horse moved at a trot along the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says RODE is said like ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotted, of a rider, means went on horseback, so rode is a fair swap.

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a penalty is coming and is told it's fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine is a sum paid as punishment and also means of good quality.

clue.text: Would this Scandinavian whisper sweet nothings?

definitions.text: Would this Scandinavian whisper sweet nothings?

parts.words: Would this Scandinavian whisper sweet nothings?
parts.note: a Scandinavian man's name that, read as a plural, also means zeros or nothings

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a Nordic man is a romantic murmurer.
explanation.walkthrough: Nils is a common Scandinavian first name; nil is nothing, so nils are nothings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is Scandinavian, and the plural of nil means nothings, so he would speak them.

clue.text: Stag arranged in jelly? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the words beside it
turns the surface round: the jelly is in the stag words, not the stag in the jelly

explanation.surface: A stag set in aspic, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'Just the opposite' point to stAG ARranged. 'arranged' looks like an anagram signal but is only part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and culture media.

clue.text: With urgency and cunning, put spear into it

indicators.note: put asks that one piece be placed somewhere, here inside the other
into it says the spear goes inside the word for cunning, the it of the clue

parts.note: sly means cunning
a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: Instructions to stab something hurriedly and craftily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the cunning word, so 'put ... into it' sends the spear inside that word. 'With urgency' reads as an instruction but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridently means in a loud, insistent manner, which conveys urgency.
